title: Exact closed functors preserve unbounded derived internal Hom
statement: Let C,D be closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions. Let F:C→D be an additive exact strong monoidal left adjoint preserving flat objects. Suppose F also has an additive exact left adjoint L, and its ordinary canonical internal-Hom comparisons F[X,Y]→[FX,FY] are isomorphisms. Then the unbounded exact derived functor D(F), with the strong monoidal structure transported from the canonical K-flat left-derived tensor comparison, has invertible canonical internal-Hom comparison at every pair of derived objects.

source.place: Tags 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U) and 07A4; exact-functor and tensor-Hom localization argument made explicit below.

proof.text: The exact left adjoint of F implies that F sends K-injective complexes to K-injectives. On complexes, ordinary closedness gives the canonical Hom-complex comparison isomorphism, using the adjunction to preserve the products in the Hom complex. Pass to the homotopy categories. The quotient functor preserves internal Hom because its closed adjunction is induced by the complex adjunction; the evaluation transpose is precisely the quotient comparison.

source.place: Tags 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U) and 07A4; exact-functor and tensor-Hom localization argument made explicit below.

proof.text: On a K-injective target, the comparison from homotopy internal Hom to derived internal Hom is invertible. Prove the factorization square for the derived functor monoidal by its canonical tensor/counit equation. Naturality and composition of internal-Hom comparisons identify the ordinary comparison transported through the quotient and localization with the derived evaluation transpose. Cancel the three known invertible arrows in this square.

proof.text: Every first derived input has a complex representative; every second input has a K-injective representative. Naturality of the canonical comparison under the two representing isomorphisms transports invertibility to every pair.
